analyst_view.overall: Early view: Hull have drawn three of their last five and defended compactly for over an hour in a 1-0 defeat at Arsenal, but key creator Mohamed Belloumi is injured and the squad has a long injury list. Forest, under Oliver Glasner, just beat Manchester City 3-1 with a hard-running pressing game. Two sides separated by two points makes this a cagey, low-margin game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals, and I agree. Hull's games average just over two goals and Belloumi, involved in five of their 11 league goals, has not trained since the Ipswich draw; Forest have scored only nine in 10. Liam Delap's two goals against City are the one sign Forest's attack is waking up.

corners.text: The site has 9.4 corners. I agree: Hull sit deep in a back five and invite crosses, while Forest's wide players like Neco Williams and Dan Ndoye supply them. Nothing points clearly either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. I lean higher: Forest's press, led by Ryan Yates and Xaver Schlager, is built on duels and fouls in midfield, and a close game between two sides near the bottom tends to be scrappy. Four bookings looks more likely than three.

shots.text: The site has 26.9 shots, with 16.9 for Forest. I lean lower: Forest won at the City Ground by running and pressing rather than by piling up shots, and Hull were hard to break down at Arsenal. This looks like a low-chance game.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.9 shots on target. I lean slightly lower because Hull are missing Belloumi and several midfielders, including Hidemasa Morita and Darko Gyabi, and Forest have been blunt for most of the season. Around seven on target fits.
